source.note: 564-278M, Specifications and Capacities table p.34. The pypdf text layer reversed several table rows character-by-character (a PDF layout/rendering artifact, e.g. "Tillage Width" came out as "htdiW egalliT") — decoded by reversing those specific lines back, and cross-checked that the recovered Tillage Width values exactly equal each SKU's own number in feet (CT8300-18 = 18ft, etc.), which they do. Transport Width, Center Section Width, and exact tire assignment are printed once per size-BLOCK in the source (not once per model) and the block boundaries were not fully recoverable from the garbled layout — omitted rather than guessed which models they cover. source.note: 596-381M, Specifications and Capacities table p.25 — the table itself is a graphic/vector table (not extractable as text via pypdf), rendered to an image at 200dpi and read visually. It's a dense 18-column grid (all combinations of 3-6 shanks x 5 spacing options) and individual per-model transport-width/frame-number cells are easy to mis-map by eye at that density. Working width was cross-checked against 3 known-good rows and equals shankSpacingIn x numberOfShanks exactly, so it's given as a formula rather than transcribed per row (removes that whole risk). Weight and HP bucket by shank count (with two sub-tiers at 5 shanks) and were verified consistent across the columns read for each bucket. Transport width, kilowatt, and internal frame-number fields were NOT transcribed — the visual density made per-column mapping unreliable enough that I'd rather omit them than risk silently-wrong numbers; re-derive from the source table image directly if needed. Despite the "VT" prefix (usually Vertical Tillage in this brand's naming) this is functionally an inline sub-soiler/ripper, not vertical tillage. (sku values were synthesized from subline/shank count/spacing because the source table lists configurations rather than model numbers.)

constants.workingWidthFormula: shankSpacingIn * numberOfShanks (confirmed against source table, not assumed)
